subdivision_of_building: REAR PART OF GROUND FLOOR AND SECOND FLOOR ROOF SPACE
description: Conversion of loft space involving a dormer extension at rear, dormer windows to front roofslope, a rooflight to rear roofslope, window to second floor flank elevation and alteration to ground floor rear fenestration to provide a self contained residential unit, demolition of the single storey rear extension and outbuildings, erection of a part one, part two storey building to rear comprising two self contained residential units and installation of air source heat pumps to ground floor flank elevation, external access stairs with refuse storage below to the front of the new building with amenity areas, new boundary treatments, car parking bay and provision of a detached cycle store to rear.
decision_conditions: The development must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date hereof.Reason: To comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended.

No development shall begin, including demolition and site clearance works, until a Construction Logistics Plan (CLP) and Construction Management Plan (CMP), to include details of: (a) loading and unloading of plant and materials; (b ) storage of plant and materials; (c) programme of works (including measures for traffic management); (d) provision of boundary hoarding, behind any visibility zones of construction traffic routing; (e) hours of operation; (f) and means to prevent deposition of mud on the highway have been submitted, to and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The development shall be constructed in accordance with the approved statement. Reason: To ensure that the proposed development does not interfere with the free flow of traffic and conditions of safety on the public highway, and to ensure the development process does not have a significant adverse impact on the amenities of nearby residential properties.

The development hereby approved shall be constructed in accordance with the details indicated in drawing number 207 Rev: A hereby approved.Reason: To safeguard the visual amenities of the area and to ensure compliance with Policies 28 and 30 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The site and building works required to implement the development shall only be carried out between the hours of 08.00 and 18.00 Mondays to Fridays, and between 08.00 and 13.00 on Saturdays, and not at all on Bank Holidays and Sundays. Reason: To protect the amenities of adjoining and nearby properties during the construction of the development hereby permitted.

Prior to the commencement of any works above ground / DPC level, a finalised Energy Statement must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing which demonstrates how each of the proposed dwellings will apply the Mayor's energy hierarchy (use less energy, supply energy efficiently and use renewable energy) to achieve the targeted reduction in CO2 emissions over and above the Part L 2021 baseline. The revised Energy Statement must incorporate:(i) roof plans showing the number of solar PV panels per dwelling and the total area of the proposed array;(ii) the sizing, positioning and orientation of the proposed air source heat pumps (ASHP) units; and(iii) 'as-designed' Standard Assessment Procedure (SAP) outputs confirming the emissions reductions to be achieved.Reason: To comply with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to first occupation, as-built' Standard Assessment Procedure (SAP) outputs must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing to demonstrate that the energy strategy has been implemented in accordance with the approved details. If the development is unable to meet the required reduction in CO2 emissions through the approved energy strategy, then any shortfall shall be made up through the application of further sustainability measures. Reason: To comply with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The development hereby approved shall be constructed in accordance with the approved Drainage Strategy Report prepared by Civil Engineering Solutions Ltd and dated April 2025. Prior to first occupation of the development, written confirmation that the approved SuDS measures, including SuDS, have been implemented as part of the development as built must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing. All of the approved measures must thereafter be retained for as long as the development is in existence. Reason: To comply with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 201

Prior to first occupation of the development, a completed Water Efficiency Calculator for New Dwellings must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing to show that internal potable water consumption for each of the dwellings will be limited to no more than 110 litres per person per day (l/p/d) based on the Government's national calculation method for the purposes of Part G of the Building Regulations.Reason: To comply with Policy 33 of the Sutton Local Plan 201

No dwelling shall be occupied until space has been laid out within the site in accordance with drawing no 203 Revision D  for bicycles to be parked witin the curtilage of the site and these spaces shall thereafter be kept available for the parking of bicycles.Reason: To ensure the development provides an adequate level of cycle parking facilities and to encourage sustainable modes of transport, in accordance with Policies 36 and 37 of the Local Plan.

No dwelling shall be occupied until space has been laid out within the site in accordance with drawing no drawing no 203 Revision D for one car to be parked within the curtilage of the site and that these spaces shall thereafter be kept available at all times for the parking of vehicles.Reason: To ensure the proposed development does not lead to an increase in on-street parking and in accordance with Policy 37 of Sutton's Local Plan 2018.

Prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved, details of the means of enclosure and boundary treatments of the private amenity space for the first floor flat shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority, and the approved details shall be implemented prior to the first occupation. The means of enclosure shall thereafter be permanently retained.Reason: To protect the amenity of the future occupiers of the development hereby approved in accordance with Policy 29 of the  Local Plan.

Prior to first occupation of the new flats, the refuse/recycling storage as indicated on drawing no: 203 Revision D shall be fully implemented and retained permanently thereafter.Reason: Reason: To ensure the development provides an adequate amount of refuse provision in accordance with Policy 5.17 of the London Plan.

The proposed side facing windows to the first and second floor flats of the development hereby approved shall be obscure glazed and non-opening up to a height of 1.7m above floor level prior to its occupation and shall be retained in that form as long as the development is in existence. The Feature Bay window to first floor side elevation shall have a 450mm wide Clear Glazed, Openable Side Windows, with Fixed Obscure Glazed Face Window.Reason: To protect the amenities of adjoining occupiers and to ensure compliance with Policy 29 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The approved mitigation measures recommended in the applications Acoustic report shall be implemented prior to beneficial occupation of the development and be permanently retained thereafter.Reason: To ensure satisfactory living conditions for the occupants of the development, in accordance with policy 29 of the Sutton's Local Plan 2018.

Apart from the private amenity space indicated, the flat roof sections of the development at first and second floor level hereby approved shall not be used, all or in part, as a terrace or other amenity space. No railings, fences, walls or other means of enclosure shall be erected on these flat roofs, and no alterations shall be carried out to the rear and side elevations of the application property to form access onto these roofs.Reason: Such a use would be harmful to the existing amenities of the occupiers of neighbouring residential properties as a result of overlooking and loss of privacy and the generation of noise and disturbance contrary to Policy 29 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.
